name: Peginterferon alfa-2a
drug_class: Pegylated type I interferon (immunomodulator and antiviral cytokine)
owner: pharma& (pharmaand GmbH; rights acquired from Roche)

discovery.note: Recombinant interferon alfa-2a attached to a branched 40 kDa polyethylene glycol, slowing clearance to allow weekly dosing.

tagline: Weekly long-acting interferon, once the backbone of hepatitis C and B treatment
summary: Peginterferon alfa-2a is recombinant interferon alfa-2a linked to a large branched polyethylene glycol molecule, which prolongs its action so it can be injected weekly. With ribavirin it was standard treatment for chronic hepatitis C for over a decade until interferon-free direct-acting antivirals replaced it. It is still used for a finite course in chronic hepatitis B and hepatitis D.
mechanism: Interferon alfa binds the type I interferon receptor (IFNAR1/IFNAR2) and activates JAK1 and TYK2, which phosphorylate STAT1 and STAT2. These form the ISGF3 complex with IRF9 and switch on hundreds of interferon-stimulated genes that inhibit viral replication, such as protein kinase R, OAS/RNase L and Mx proteins.

Interferon also enhances antigen presentation and the activity of natural killer cells and cytotoxic T cells. Pegylation increases molecular size, reducing renal clearance and giving sustained blood levels.
uses: Chronic hepatitis B (HBeAg-positive and negative) in adults and children
Chronic hepatitis C in combination with ribavirin or other antivirals (now rarely used)
Chronic hepatitis D (off-label in many countries)

history.title: Approval
history.detail: Pegasys is approved in the EU in June 2002 and by the FDA in October 2002 for chronic hepatitis C.

history.title: Combination with ribavirin
history.detail: Pegasys plus ribavirin becomes a standard regimen for hepatitis C; approval for hepatitis B follows in 2005.

history.title: Hepatitis B
history.detail: Pegasys is approved in the US for chronic hepatitis B.

history.title: Triple therapy
history.detail: First-generation HCV protease inhibitors (telaprevir, boceprevir) are approved for use with peginterferon and ribavirin.

history.title: Decline in HCV
history.detail: Interferon-free regimens largely end peginterferon use for hepatitis C.

pk.half_life: about 80 h (range 50–140 h) after subcutaneous injection
pk.metabolism: proteolysis; the large PEG reduces renal clearance

safety.boxed_warning: May cause or aggravate fatal or life-threatening neuropsychiatric, autoimmune, ischaemic and infectious disorders; monitor closely and withdraw for persistently severe or worsening signs (US label).

facts: Peginterferon alfa-2a uses a 40 kDa branched PEG, whereas peginterferon alfa-2b uses a 12 kDa linear PEG.
A 48-week course of peginterferon is the only finite therapy for hepatitis B that can lead to HBsAg loss in a minority of patients.
